slides.title: Overview of the various operational and financial considerations regarding the lane pricing review for the upcoming fiscal year planning cycle
bullets: Operating margin has declined from 7.8% to 4.9% over the last two fiscal years even though total shipment volume grew by 11% across all regions and customer segments
A small number of lanes appear to be responsible for the majority of the losses, but the exact figures depend on how shared overhead costs are allocated across the network
Competitor pricing on comparable lanes appears to be higher than ours by a meaningful margin according to broker benchmarks and several publicly available tariff filings
Customers have indicated in interviews that they value guaranteed capacity and predictable surcharges more than the absolute price level on the most congested lanes
Any pricing change would need to be coordinated with the contract renewal calendar, the sales compensation plan, and the customer communications team
There are additional considerations regarding fuel surcharges, accessorial charges, and minimum-volume commitments that should be reviewed as part of this work
The finance team has also raised questions about the impact on working capital and on the timing of revenue recognition for multi-year contracts
